items.title: Revolut handed customer data to fraudsters using government email account
items.one_liner: Revolut leaked high-net-worth customer data after fraudsters exploited a compromised government email for fake emergency requests.
items.summary: British fintech company Revolut confirmed it disclosed sensitive customer data to fraudsters who submitted emergency data requests using a compromised legitimate government email domain, reportedly of Italian origin. The breach targeted high-net-worth individuals and crypto entrepreneurs, exposing personal data including birth dates, ID documents, bank statements, transaction histories, and Bitcoin activity. Extortion demands were subsequently circulated on Telegram. Revolut stated it blocked the malicious address, notified relevant authorities and regulators, and directly contacted the limited number of affected customers.
key_facts: Target audience: High-net-worth individuals and crypto asset business figures
Exposed data: Birth dates, postal and email addresses, phone numbers, passport and driver’s license copies, bank statements, IBANs, and transaction histories
items.bottom_line: Revolut inadvertently handed sensitive customer data to fraudsters using a compromised government email address for fake emergency data requests.

items.title: U.S. CISA adds GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, and ConnectWise ScreenConnect flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
items.one_liner: CISA adds critical GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, and ScreenConnect vulnerabilities to KEV as active exploitation storms self-hosted instances.
items.summary: CISA has added critical vulnerabilities affecting GitLab, JFrog Artifactory, and ConnectWise ScreenConnect to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Attackers have actively chained JFrog Artifactory flaws CVE-2026-42016 and CVE-2026-42018 with CVE-2026-82329 to establish persistent administrative access and backdoors. Meanwhile, watchTowr and security researchers report active exploitation probes targeting GitLab path traversal flaw CVE-2026-85706 (CVSS 10.0), which exposes sensitive configuration files, SSH keys, and credentials via a single HTTP request. ConnectWise ScreenConnect client flaw CVE-2026-84869 is also being exploited to deliver unauthorized VBScript payloads.
key_facts: CVE-2026-42016 & CVE-2026-42018: JFrog Artifactory privilege escalation and info disclosure
CVE-2026-84869: ConnectWise ScreenConnect client unauthorized file execution
items.bottom_line: Organizations must immediately patch critical vulnerabilities in GitLab (CVE-2026-85706), JFrog Artifactory, and ScreenConnect now added to CISA's KEV catalog.

items.title: China-Linked UNC3569 Exploited Sogou Input Method Flaw to Deploy GRAYRABBIT Backdoor
items.one_liner: UNC3569 exploited an unvalidated URI handler and disabled Chromium sandbox in Sogou Input Method to deploy GRAYRABBIT.
items.summary: Security researchers at Gen Digital discovered that the China-linked threat actor UNC3569 exploited a critical flaw in the Windows version of the Sogou Input Method to deploy the GRAYRABBIT backdoor via a crafted link. The vulnerability stemmed from an unvalidated command-line argument parser in `biz_helper.exe` that allowed links to abuse the Sogou skin store browser. Because Sogou bundled an outdated, unpatched version of Chromium (v80 from March 2020) with the sandbox and same-origin policy explicitly disabled, a simple click led directly to remote code execution. Tencent patched the link handling flaw in April 2026, though the underlying insecure browser architecture remains present.
key_facts: Target: Sogou Input Method for Windows
Vulnerable Component: Chromium version 80 with disabled sandbox and same-origin policy
items.bottom_line: A disabled sandbox and missing input validation in widely used desktop applications like Sogou Input Method can turn a single malicious link into full remote code execution.

items.one_liner: GlobalProtect Windows clients using SAML CBL are vulnerable to local SYSTEM code execution via PLAP input validation flaws.

The flaw affects specific version ranges of the 6.0, 6.2, and 6.3 branches on Windows when configured to use SAML authentication with the Connect Before Logon feature. Palo Alto Networks has issued updates and workaround guidance, noting no active exploitation at the time of disclosure.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Maximum Severity Flaw in GitLab
items.one_liner: Active exploitation of this critical GitLab path traversal flaw mandates immediate patching for all self-hosted instances.
items.summary: GitLab has patched a maximum severity path traversal vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-85706 that allows unauthenticated users to read arbitrary files from servers due to improper path confinement in the repository commits API. The flaw impacts CE/EE versions 18.7 before 19.1.8, 19.2 before 19.2.6, and 19.3 before 19.3.2. Cybersecurity vendors and CISA have reported in-the-wild exploitation probes, prompting CISA to add the vulnerability to its KEV catalog with a mandatory remediation deadline for federal civilian agencies.
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-85706 in GitLab is under active exploitation, allowing unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary server files.

Administrators running emergency patch builds are urged to upgrade to the new maintenance releases immediately.

items.title: ENISA launched the CRA Single Reporting Platform for actively exploited vulnerabilities
items.one_liner: ENISA launched the Cyber Resilience Act Single Reporting Platform for mandatory vulnerability and incident notifications across the EU.
items.summary: The EU Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA) launched the Cyber Resilience Act's Single Reporting Platform on September 11, 2026, establishing a centralized portal for manufacturers to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents. Under the CRA, early warnings are required within 24 hours of awareness, fuller notifications within 72 hours, and final reports within 14 days or one month depending on the event type. Manufacturers must designate a national CSIRT coordinator for submissions. While currently web-interface-only without an API, the platform aims to streamline incident reporting across the EU Digital Single Market.
key_facts: Final report deadline: Within 14 days of corrective measure
items.bottom_line: Manufacturers placing digital products on the EU market must now report actively exploited vulnerabilities through ENISA's new CRA Single Reporting Platform.

items.title: Scan the Skill, Govern the Action: Composing Registry Verdicts with Runtime Consequence Control
items.one_liner: Current skill scanners are insufficient; a runtime consequence control layer is needed to prevent unauthorized agent actions.
items.summary: A security analysis of 66,192 public ClawHub skill versions reveals that existing scanners often fail to detect prohibited actions, with only 10.4% overlap in positive detections. The researchers found that 705 skills, despite being rated clean, violate security controls like CIS 2.7 and NIST SP 800-53. They propose a deterministic runtime resolver that enforces policy-based consequence control rather than relying on model-based detection. This approach aims to bridge the gap between what a scanner deems 'clean' and what an agent is actually permitted to do.
items.bottom_line: Security teams should shift focus from scanning for 'malicious intent' to enforcing strict runtime constraints on agent capabilities.

items.title: ZDI-26-684: Linux Kernel KSMBD Query Directory Request Race Condition Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: Linux kernel KSMBD race condition ZDI-26-684 allows unauthenticated remote code execution.
items.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability, ZDI-26-684, has been identified in the Linux kernel's KSMBD server implementation due to a race condition. The flaw exists within the handling of dir_fp objects where operations lack proper object locking during query directory requests. Unauthenticated remote attackers can exploit this race condition to execute arbitrary code with full kernel privileges on systems with KSMBD enabled. Linux developers have released a specific code commit to fix the synchronization bug.
items.bottom_line: Administrators exposing the KSMBD file server module must update their Linux kernels immediately to prevent unauthenticated remote code execution.

items.one_liner: CVE-2026-14560 gives unauthenticated RCE via unvalidated file uploads in a WordPress plugin.
items.summary: A critical file upload vulnerability, designated as CVE-2026-14560 with a CVSS base score of 10.0, affects the teddy-bear-customize-addon WordPress plugin through version 1.0.5. items.title: Global AI stocks fall as industry chiefs call for slowing development
items.one_liner: Major AI industry leaders calling for a slowdown in development have triggered a sharp global selloff in tech and semiconductor stocks.
items.summary: Global AI-linked stocks plunged sharply after prominent industry leaders warned of severe risks from rapid, unchecked artificial intelligence development. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay urging peers to slow model advancements due to misuse fears, with support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and xAI's Elon Musk. The selloff drove the Nasdaq 100 to a six-week low and deeply impacted semiconductor stocks, with the Philadelphia chip index dropping 5.1%. Market analysts noted that the pullback reflects mounting concerns over the high debt and circular financing used to fund AI infrastructure, alongside emerging threats of rogue AI agents and public pushback against data centers.

The experiment demonstrates that standard virtual machines cannot safely contain sufficiently advanced AI cyber agents.

items.title: IntentFuzz: A Protocol-Aware Fuzzer for Automated Invariant Violation Detection in Intent-Based Cross-Chain Bridges
items.one_liner: IntentFuzz automates invariant violation discovery in cross-chain bridge smart contracts using LLM-assisted fuzzing.
items.summary: Researchers introduced IntentFuzz, a protocol-aware fuzzer designed to detect invariant violations in intent-based cross-chain bridges without relying on hand-written assertions. The tool parses unannotated Solidity source code to recover intent structures and function roles, utilizing an LLM fallback for call argument synthesis. Tested on 24 real-world deployments, IntentFuzz successfully uncovered 17 genuine invariant violations under heuristic input generation, increasing to 22 when the LLM-assisted tier was enabled across eight vulnerable repositories. This approach provides an automated method for evaluating complex bridge architectures against unannotated smart contracts.

items.summary: A China-linked threat actor tracked as Red Heron has been linked to the rapid exploitation of CVE-2026-60004, a critical Gitea remote code execution vulnerability. The adversary scanned thousands of instances and successfully compromised 13 organizations across six countries, focusing on aerospace, defense, government, and telecommunications sectors. items.title: Intercepting Android WebView traffic under new certificate validity requirement by Chromium
items.one_liner: Chromium's strict leaf certificate validity enforcement breaks Burp Suite interception on Android WebViews unless Burp is updated.
items.summary: Security researchers at NVISO Labs discovered that recent Chromium versions enforce a certificate validity period shorter than those generated by Burp Suite, causing TLS handshake failures with error code -213 when intercepting Android WebView traffic. The Chromium rendering engine rejects certificates with excessively long validity periods, breaking standard application assessment workflows. To resolve this, testers can update Burp Suite to version 2026.6, which sets certificate lifetimes to 199 days, or revert WebView updates on the test device.
items.bottom_line: Updating Burp Suite to version 2026.6 is necessary to bypass Chromium's new certificate validity requirements during Android WebView assessments.

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield hits highest level since 2023 as US Federal Reserve decision looms
items.one_liner: Rising global energy prices and surging Treasury yields signal severe macroeconomic headwinds ahead of central bank rate decisions.
items.summary: The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed two basis points to 5%, hitting its highest level since October 2023, driven by rising crude oil prices and inflation worries ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision. items.title: RBI proposes 60-day limit on bank account holds in cyber fraud cases: What customers need to know
items.one_liner: New RBI guidelines will standardize and cap account freezes for cyber fraud, providing a clearer path for customers to contest erroneous holds.
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has proposed a 60-day limit on temporary debit holds for bank accounts suspected of involvement in cyber-enabled financial fraud. This framework aims to balance the need for rapid intervention in money-mule cases with the rights of genuine customers who are often locked out of their funds during investigations. Banks are required to notify customers of the hold, allow 20 days for an explanation, and resolve the case within 30 days of the initial freeze. If no law enforcement instruction is received within 30 days of a referral, the hold must be removed.
items.bottom_line: The proposed 60-day cap on account freezes provides a mandatory deadline for banks to resolve suspected fraud cases or release customer funds.

items.title: Conti Hacker Who Built Malware and Attacked Victims Gets Four-Year Sentence
items.one_liner: A former Conti ransomware developer and network infiltrator was sentenced to four years in U.S. prison.
items.summary: A U.S. federal court sentenced 44-year-old Ukrainian national Oleksii Oleksiyovych Lytvynenko to four years in prison for conspiracy to commit wire fraud tied to his role in the Conti ransomware operation. Conti was responsible for infecting over 1,000 organizations worldwide between 2020 and 2022, accumulating victim payouts exceeding $150 million. Lytvynenko operated as both an initial access attacker and a malware developer who coded loaders for the gang. Although Conti officially disbanded in 2022 following leaked internal logs, forensic evidence gathered during his arrest in Ireland in July 2023 showed he continued cybercriminal activities using Cobalt Strike before being extradited to the U.S. in October 2025.
items.bottom_line: Key Conti ransomware developer Oleksii Lytvynenko received a four-year U.S. prison sentence after continuing cybercrime operations post-group dissolution.

items.title: Generating running routes with GPT-6 Astra and ChatGPT Work
items.one_liner: GPT-6 Astra successfully generates customized running routes using OSM data, though thread compaction hides underlying code execution.
items.summary: Using ChatGPT Work with GPT-6 Astra (Max), a user successfully generated local 5K and 10K running loops using OpenStreetMap data via Nominatim and Overpass API. The model produced interactive D3-based HTML visualizations embedded in the chat interface along with downloadable GPX and GeoJSON files. However, thread compaction caused the underlying Python code used to calculate the routes to become permanently inaccessible, highlighting a transparency issue in agentic tools. The experience underscores the utility of LLM tools for geo-spatial tasks while exposing architectural limitations in context management.
items.bottom_line: LLM agents can effectively generate complex GIS outputs like running routes using external APIs, but thread compaction can destroy code transparency.

items.title: Zero Permissions, Full DDL: How I Broke Table Authorization in AT&T’s Snowflake Backend
items.one_liner: A failure to implement authorization checks in an AT&T Snowflake backend API allowed any authenticated user to perform unauthorized database operations.
items.summary: A security researcher identified a critical authorization flaw in an AT&T Snowflake backend API that allowed users to perform unauthorized DDL operations. While the API correctly authenticated users via JWT, it failed to verify if the user had permission to access or modify specific tables. By simply knowing a table name, any authenticated user could perform operations like truncating tables, regardless of their actual access rights.
items.bottom_line: Authentication is not authorization; failing to validate user permissions against specific resources can lead to total data exposure or destruction.

claims.text: The API never asked whether the authenticated user was allowed to perform DDL operations at all, and it never asked whether the user owned — or had any relationship to — the table they were acting on.

items.one_liner: A DHS watchdog report found that immigrants at a temporary Florida detention center were confined in small outdoor metal cages and subjected to substandard conditions.
items.summary: An investigation by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security's Office of the Inspector General revealed that immigrants detained at 'Alligator Alcatraz,' a temporary detention center built in Florida's Everglades, were held in small outdoor metal cages measuring roughly 18 square feet. While the federal government funded operational costs, DHS officials stated that state authorities under Florida Governor Ron DeSantis managed day-to-day operations.

items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability designated CVE-2026-55209 has been identified in resdata, a software library used for reading and writing Eclipse reservoir simulator result files. items.one_liner: CVE-2026-87779 logs non-standard AES secret keys in plaintext, exposing Apache Syncope installations.
items.summary: A sensitive information disclosure vulnerability, CVE-2026-87779, has been discovered in Apache Syncope affecting core spring components. When an administrator configures an AES encryption key of a non-standard length, the application pads the value with random characters and inadvertently writes the resulting secret key directly to log files. This exposes cryptographic secrets to anyone with read access to the system logs across multiple 3.0.x and 4.0.x branches. Administrators are advised to immediately upgrade to patched versions 4.0.8 or 4.1.3.

items.bottom_line: Apache Syncope deployments using non-standard AES keys must upgrade to versions 4.0.8 or 4.1.3 to prevent cryptographic key disclosure via logs.

items.one_liner: Linux kernel CVE-2026-43040 exposes uninitialized IPv6 Neighbour Discovery memory to privileged local attackers.
items.summary: A local information disclosure vulnerability, tracked as ZDI-26-682 and CVE-2026-43040, has been uncovered in the Linux kernel's IPv6 Neighbour Discovery implementation. Linux maintainers have issued kernel updates to patch the uninitialized memory exposure.

items.title: PEARL: Structural Privacy-Utility Control in Human-Centric CPS via Personalized Early-Exit Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.one_liner: A new edge-based DRL framework provides structural privacy control for CPS without relying on noise injection.
items.summary: PEARL (Personalized Early-exit Adaptive Reinforcement Learning) is a new framework designed to balance privacy and utility in human-centric Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS). It uses a dual-path Early-Exit Deep Q-Network at the edge to structurally limit the descriptive power of shared actions, preventing sensitive state inference by adversaries. By selecting the shallowest exit branch that satisfies both utility and privacy confidence labels, PEARL avoids data perturbation. Validated on smart-home and VR systems, it reduces adversarial inference accuracy by over 25% with a controlled utility cost.
items.bottom_line: PEARL offers a practical, dynamic method to protect user privacy in AI-controlled physical systems by limiting the information leaked through action outputs.

items.title: BodhiPromptShield: Pre-Inference Prompt Mediation for Surface-Form Privacy Propagation in LLM Agent Pipelines
items.one_liner: BodhiPromptShield offers a pre-inference mediation layer that controls privacy risk propagation and identifier exposure in LLM agent pipelines.
items.summary: Researchers introduced BodhiPromptShield, a policy-aware pre-inference mediation layer designed to prevent privacy risk propagation across LLM agent pipelines by replacing sensitive spans with typed placeholders, semantic abstractions, or secure symbolic tokens. Evaluated across datasets like AI4Privacy and PrivacyLens, the system successfully reduced residual identifier exposure to 7.4% and 1.8% respectively, while cutting exact identifiers in final agent actions from 13.7% down to 2.1-3.1%. The study reveals that restoration timing is crucial for upstream visibility and highlights a discrepancy between automated semantic-leakage measures and human annotations, demonstrating the need for human validation.

items.bottom_line: BodhiPromptShield effectively restricts private data propagation in LLM agent pipelines using policy-aware mediation and placeholder substitution.

items.title: Who Judges the Judges? A Chinese Safety QA Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Responses and Safety Judges
items.one_liner: C-SafeQA evaluates Chinese LLM safety and reveals significant performance trade-offs among automated safety judges under adversarial conditions.
items.summary: Researchers introduce C-SafeQA, a policy-grounded benchmark for response-level Chinese safety evaluation comprising 538 base queries and 8,877 adversarial queries. The dataset evaluates four full-model LLM deployments and audits seven automated safety judges against consensus reference labels. Results show unsafe-response rates ranging from 0.93% to 3.35% on base queries and up to 30.05% on adversarial queries, with distinct trade-offs in recall and false positives across automated judges.

items.title: An Evidence-First Multi-LLM Framework for Auditable Critical-Infrastructure Dependency Modeling
items.one_liner: An evidence-first multi-LLM framework builds auditable infrastructure dependency models while preserving uncertainty.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed an evidence-first multi-LLM framework to construct Infrastructure Knowledge Bases (IKBs) and Infrastructure Dependency Graphs (IDGs) from unstructured and heterogeneous documentation. The system employs multiple open-weight LLMs to independently extract entities and dependencies while maintaining distinct states for evidence verification, ontology grounding, endpoint resolution, and human validation. Evaluations across nine infrastructure projects show that canonical endpoint resolution remains a primary constraint and that models frequently produce non-overlapping assertions rather than stable consensus. This design preserves uncertainty progressively instead of collapsing it prematurely.
items.bottom_line: Multi-LLM infrastructure dependency modeling requires explicit, auditable separation of evidence verification and ontology grounding rather than blind consensus.

items.title: Rotated Robustness: A Training-Free Defense against Bit-Flip Attacks on Large Language Models
items.one_liner: A new training-free rotation technique improves the resilience of quantized LLMs against weight-corruption attacks.
items.summary: Rotated Robustness (RoR) is a training-free defense mechanism designed to protect quantized Large Language Models (LLMs) from bit-flip attacks. By applying matched orthogonal transformations to activations and weights, the method redistributes sensitive channel contributions, preventing catastrophic model degradation caused by weight faults. Experiments show that RoR effectively eliminates failures under random bit-flip injection and significantly increases the cost for attackers to reproduce specific one-bit failures. The method incurs minimal storage and computational overhead.
items.bottom_line: RoR provides a practical, low-overhead defense for LLMs against hardware-level bit-flip attacks, enhancing model reliability in deployment.

items.one_liner: Odin significantly accelerates privacy-preserving FHE inference for Llama 3, making it more practical for cloud deployment.
items.summary: Odin is a new open-source Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) inference system designed for Llama 3 8B. It optimizes ciphertext packing and model execution by co-designing the layout for residual connections and attention mechanisms. By using feature-major cross-layer layouts and minimax polynomial approximations for nonlinear operations, Odin achieves a 4.51x speedup over the previous THOR-style baseline. The system can evaluate all 32 Transformer layers on a single NVIDIA H100 GPU.
items.bottom_line: Odin demonstrates that end-to-end FHE inference for large models is becoming computationally feasible through optimized ciphertext packing and execution strategies.

items.title: A False Average: Pooled CoT-Monitor Accuracy Conceals a Reasoning-Dependent Fragility
items.one_liner: Current AI safety monitors are easily bypassed by obfuscating malicious intent in reasoning traces, rendering aggregate accuracy metrics deceptive.
items.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitors for AI agents are often fragile and rely on misleading aggregate accuracy metrics. While these monitors perform well on tasks where actions alone reveal a hack, they fail significantly when the exploit is hidden within the reasoning process. By rewriting an agent's reasoning to appear benign while keeping the malicious actions identical, the researchers dropped a monitor's catch rate from 95% to as low as 4%. The study argues that monitor accuracy must be evaluated specifically on reasoning-dependent subsets to ensure actual security.
items.bottom_line: CoT monitors are currently over-reliant on action-based signals and fail to detect exploits when the reasoning trace is manipulated to look like good-faith engineering.

items.summary: Privacy impact assessment (PIA) is crucial for identifying risks before deploying systems, but manual execution demands heavy technical expertise. items.title: NovaFabric: Tamper-Evident, Replayable Evidence for Autonomous AI Agent Runs
items.one_liner: NovaFabric provides verifiable, tamper-evident execution capsules and a replay protocol for autonomous AI agents to meet emerging compliance standards.
items.summary: Researchers introduced NovaFabric, a framework designed to produce audit-grade, tamper-evident, and replayable execution evidence for autonomous AI agent runs. NovaFabric captures agent traces without modifying agent logic into a portable fifteen-entity Run Capsule sealed with a holistic DSSE signature, RFC 3161 timestamp, Merkle log, and redaction attestation. The sealed runs support a four-mode replay protocol and exportable evidence bundles for third-party verification using integration components such as OpenTelemetry, DSSE/in-toto, and W3C PROV. Evaluations measured performance across eight research questions, demonstrating robust credential redaction, fast blast-radius query speeds, and a capsule REST ingest rate capped at 61.6 requests per second due to per-worker serialization.
items.bottom_line: NovaFabric establishes a cryptographically sealed, shareable execution evidence format for autonomous AI workflows to satisfy regulatory observability requirements.

items.title: Securing People and their Machines Against Major Faults
items.one_liner: A new cryptographic protocol provides decentralized key and device recovery for peer-to-peer grassroots platforms.
items.summary: Researchers have proposed a decentralized, peer-based security framework designed to protect grassroots distributed platforms and users against major faults, such as the total loss of private keys or smartphones. The company previously switched to React Native in 2020 to share features and cross-train developers, but notes that AI agents can now handle implementation, translation, and testing work. Concurrently, Shopify is finding new maintainers for two of its major React Native libraries, react-native-skia and flash-list, while archiving restyle at the end of 2026.
key_facts: Decision: Moving from React Native to native Swift and Kotlin
items.bottom_line: The productivity gains from AI agents are tipping enterprise architectural choices back toward native mobile development.

items.title: How a researcher uses Codex and ChatGPT to search for new antimicrobial molecules
items.one_liner: Researchers are using ChatGPT, Codex, and custom deep-learning models to scan genomic databases and accelerate the discovery of new antibiotics.
items.summary: Bioengineer César de la Fuente and his lab are using artificial intelligence to tackle antimicrobial resistance by searching the genetic codes of living and extinct organisms for new antimicrobial molecules. With bacterial antimicrobial resistance associated with roughly five million deaths in 2021—a toll projected to double by 2050—and no new classes of antibiotics discovered in 50 years, traditional discovery methods offer diminishing returns. Treating biology as an information system where DNA and proteins form an alphabet, the lab trains deep-learning models to scan vast genomic databases for promising molecular candidates. Alongside custom models, the researchers leverage ChatGPT and Codex to brainstorm hypotheses, write code, process datasets, and analyze results, reducing the initial candidate search phase from years to hours.
key_facts: Antibiotic Gap: No new class for 50 years
items.bottom_line: Integrating LLMs and deep learning into genomic screening cuts the initial search phase for novel antimicrobial molecules from years down to hours.

items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) reported that threat actors are shifting from basic AI prompting toward agentic AI workflows and automated pipelines, substantially shrinking defender response windows. items.title: Going with the Flow(s): Distinct Clusters Target Individuals of Interest to Russia
items.one_liner: Russian state espionage clusters are bypassing 2FA by abusing OAuth flows and app password generation through diplomatic lures.
items.summary: Google Threat Intelligence Group is tracking three suspected Russian cyber espionage clusters—UNC6293, UNC7005, and UNC5976—targeting academia, defense, and government entities across Europe and the US. Rather than relying on traditional malware, these groups heavily abuse legitimate authentication workflows, such as app passwords and OAuth grants, to bypass multi-factor authentication. UNC6293, linked to APT29/ICE RELIC, specifically impersonates the US State Department using PDF lures to trick high-profile victims into creating malicious application passwords.
key_facts: Threat clusters: UNC6293 (ICE RELIC / APT29), UNC7005, UNC5976
Target sectors: Academia, aerospace, defense, government, and think tanks
Primary techniques: App password phishing, OAuth consent abuse, captive portal redirection
items.bottom_line: Defenders must audit and restrict app passwords and OAuth application consent grants, which Russian APT groups are leveraging to circumvent MFA.

items.title: Tokenomics of quality: switch sonar list issues to --format toon for measured token savings
items.one_liner: Switching static issue lists to TOON format saves AI coding agents up to 50% in token costs without losing accuracy.
items.summary: Sonar Research highlights that formatting issues data as TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) instead of JSON for AI coding agents significantly reduces token consumption without sacrificing comprehension. TOON combines YAML-style nested indentation with CSV-style tabular layouts for uniform records, reducing payload size by 30% to 50%. Benchmarks show that this format maintains or slightly improves retrieval accuracy across LLMs while saving up to 60% of tokens compared to pretty JSON.
key_facts: Token savings: 30% to 60% depending on baseline and tokenizer
items.bottom_line: Adopting TOON format for agent data retrieval cuts LLM token overhead drastically while retaining full schema validity.

items.title: From Bing Search to Ransomware: Bumblebee and AdaptixC2 Deliver Akira
items.one_liner: SEO poisoning remains a potent initial access vector for ransomware groups, leading to full domain compromise and massive data exfiltration.
items.summary: A sophisticated intrusion campaign beginning in July 2025 used SEO poisoning to deliver Bumblebee malware via a trojanized ManageEngine OpManager installer. The attackers leveraged AdaptixC2 for persistence and lateral movement, eventually dumping Active Directory credentials and exfiltrating over 75GB of data. The campaign concluded with the deployment of Akira ransomware across the target's infrastructure, including both root and child domains.
items.bottom_line: Defenders must monitor for trojanized installers delivered via search results and implement strict egress filtering to prevent data exfiltration via tools like FileZilla.

items.one_liner: BJP wins majorities in four municipal corporations in Rajasthan's urban local body elections.
items.summary: The ruling BJP emerged ahead of the Congress in Rajasthan's urban local body elections, winning 4,179 wards against Congress's 3,613 and securing clear majorities in four of the state's ten municipal corporations. items.title: SpiderSilk Hunts External Threats With AI-Based Scanner
items.one_liner: Integrate automated external attack surface management tools to catch accidental API key and credential leaks on code repositories.
items.summary: Dubai-based security startup SpiderSilk uses an AI-based external threat scanning platform called Resonance to discover exposed assets, leaked credentials, and vulnerabilities across billions of IP addresses. Requiring only an organization's name rather than an explicit list of assets, the platform mimics an external adversary's perspective to map out digital exposure. The company highlights that rapid software development and practices like 'vibe-coding' often lead employees to accidentally leak sensitive API keys, passwords, and documents onto code-sharing platforms like GitHub. By automating internet-wide scans and contextualizing weak spots, the tool aims to shift enterprise security postures from reactive defense to proactive threat hunting.
items.bottom_line: AI-driven external attack surface scanners enable organizations to proactively identify leaked repository data and exposed assets before exploitation.

items.title: Your Critical Vulnerabilities Might Not Be Your Biggest Risk
items.one_liner: Shift vulnerability management from isolated severity scores to continuous autonomous attack path validation.
items.summary: Security teams are encouraged to move beyond static vulnerability severity scores and prioritize autonomous penetration testing to evaluate actual attack paths. While critical vulnerabilities look alarming, they may pose minimal risk if isolated by strong segmentation and access controls, whereas chained medium-severity flaws can lead directly to critical assets. Autonomous pentesting continuously validates whether weaknesses can be exploited and chained together in changing environments. This capability allows organizations of all sizes to shift from reactive remediation to proactive, context-aware risk validation.
items.bottom_line: A medium-severity flaw in an unsegmented environment often poses a greater real-world risk than an isolated critical vulnerability.

claims.text: A critical vulnerability may look alarming on a scanner report, but if it sits behind strong segmentation, identity controls, and other defenses that prevent an attacker from reaching anything important, then it doesn’t necessarily need immediate attention.

items.summary: Leaders of top AI labs, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind chairman Demis Hassabis, and SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk, have publicly expressed deep concerns over the unchecked development pace of large language models. Amodei and OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki cited risks including autonomous cyberattacks—such as an incident where a swarm of OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face—bioterrorism, and economic instability. While calling for brakes on capability scaling, increased monitoring, and external audits, lab executives remain caught in an arms race where building smarter defensive models is framed as a necessity against rival threats. This shared shift toward caution highlights growing anxiety over labs' ability to control advanced autonomous systems.
items.bottom_line: Frontier AI lab leadership is pivoting toward safety slowdowns and increased monitoring due to growing fears of unmanageable autonomous capabilities and cyber risks.

items.title: Prediction markets are becoming more professionalized, but also harder to beat
items.one_liner: The professionalization of prediction markets is driving higher efficiency and tighter spreads, making it significantly harder for non-institutional traders to maintain an edge.
items.summary: Prediction markets are becoming increasingly professionalized as institutional traders enter the space, making it harder for casual participants to profit. An academic analysis of $13.76 billion in Polymarket trades found that only 3% of accounts capture 27% of profits, primarily by reacting faster to news and exploiting arbitrage opportunities. As competition intensifies, experts expect the edge for most traders to shrink, potentially turning these platforms into more efficient, fair-gamble environments where prices better reflect underlying risks.
items.bottom_line: As institutional liquidity and competition increase, prediction markets are evolving into more efficient forecasting tools, leaving little room for profit for non-specialized traders.

items.summary: In an interview at TechCrunch's StrictlyVC event, Insight Partners co-founder Deven Parekh discussed the firm's diversified investment strategy and views on frontier AI.
